channel.title: The Awesome Ledger — awesome-zsh-plugins
channel.description: New entries across the GitHub awesome ecosystem, diffed nightly.

item.title: hi-shell — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Generates shell commands from natural-language requests and shows them as reviewable inline suggestions in ZSH.

item.title: smart-complete — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A modern smart completion & suggestion layer for ZSH. Replaces both zsh-autocomplete and zsh-autosuggestions in a single plugin.

item.title: gitspace — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Binds a git identity to a directory. The wrong account fails loudly instead of signing a commit quietly.

item.title: chuchu — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Tints your terminal background by where you are. When you step into a pod, a container or a remote host, the pane's background turns a color derived from that name, and goes back once you return to the prompt. The same name always gets the same color, so you learn to recognise places at a glance.

item.title: zshist — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A shell history daemon-free replacement for ZSH's built-in history. Stores every command in a JSONL file with directory, exit code, timestamp, and duration, and gives you fzf-powered fuzzy search plus prefix-based up-arrow-style search.

item.title: tssh — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Adds a function for connecting to a named tmux session on a remote host. selects the tmux integration mode from the current terminal - tmux control mode for iTerm 2, standard tmux client for everything else.

item.title: guesswork — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Fish-style history autosuggestions ranked by an AI model instead of prefix matching, so an abbreviation or a short description of what you want finds the right command out of your recent history.

item.title: yazi — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: a tiny plugin for yazi integration.

item.title: worktree-jump — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Lists git worktrees in a compact table and lets you jump to one by typing its number at the next shell prompt.

item.title: termrec — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: This hook enables termrec to split the session into per-command sections while it generates a command-aware transcript.

item.title: terminal-pet — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Hooks preexec/precmd up to terminal-pet, an animated pixel-art pet that sits on your terminal window and reacts to your commands (macOS).

item.title: pyroclear — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A terminal clear replacement that burns your screen down before wiping it.

item.title: port — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A minimal theme combining the robbyrussell layout with the gentoo git workflow. Built on ZSH's built-in vcs_info — no external dependencies, no prompt frameworks required. Shows the current directory, version-control state (Git and SVN), and command exit status in a single compact line.

item.title: herdr — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Manages herdr agent management.

item.title: corbon — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A lightweight, highly customizable theme that gives you control over the layout, segments, Git information, colors, symbols, path display, command timing, and more without turning configuration into a mess.

item.title: boot-kit — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Adds instrumentation to your ZSH environment.

item.title: awesome-lazy-zsh — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: automates your ZSH setup with 46 plugins, 5 themes, configuration profiles, and service installation. It installs dependencies, manages Oh My Zsh, and gives you a beautiful interactive CLI to build the terminal environment you want.

item.title: nick — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A Powerline-style ZSH theme derived from agnoster, with a git segment that never blocks the prompt. Includes decorators for exit status, job count, user@host, git status, node version and current directory.

item.title: katana — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A minimalist, samurai-inspired prompt theme. Renders the current directory and Git branch/status as two compact, dark steel-toned segments, joined by a Powerline-style separator, with a single crimson accent used for Git status.

item.title: apple-userhost — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: 2-line prompt with an Apple icon. Includes decorators for user@hostname, current directory and git status

item.title: worktrunk — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Inspired by the oh-my-zsh git plugin and provides aliases and a few useful functions for working with worktrunk.

item.title: ssh-git-operations — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Provides secure, authenticated git push/pull/fetch operations over SSH to remote machines using GitHub token authentication. Tokens are never persisted on remote machines.

item.title: histpop — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Removes the last record from ~/.zsh_history. Useful right after running a command you don't want kept in your shell history (e.g. one containing a typo'd password or a temporary secret). Running histpop itself is also removed from history, so it leaves no trace.

item.title: git-branch — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Augments git features, designed especially for users who prefer aesthetically pleasing branch naming conventions. It visually formats the current git branch name or commit hash, considering customisable variables like hiding status, maximum branch length, prefix, and suffix trimming, with an option to display git status.

item.title: cage — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Adds command for age. It encrypts a plain file with a passphrase, decrypts an age file, and works out which from the file's own header.

item.title: psmon — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Lightweight interactive process monitor using standard Linux utilities (ps, awk, lsof) with live watch mode, resource sorting, and tree-aware process killing.

item.title: mtsh — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Multi-line prompt for multi-user and DevOps machines. Includes decorators for the date and time, the address of the interface that reaches the default route, CPU and memory use, the number of logged-in users, git branch and status, and the exit code and duration of the last command. No fonts are required.

item.title: dual-history — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Keeps AI coding agent instructions (such as Forge's :-prefixed prompts) out of your main ZSH history by routing them to a separate file, intercepting every write path including the agent's own history insertions. Also turns Ctrl+R into an fzf interface switchable between All, Human and AI views, merged chronologically.

item.title: deja — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: Predicts the command you want to run from fuzzy matching, the current directory, and which command usually follows the previous one, then shows it as inline ghost text. Backed by a Go daemon.

item.title: ansible-fzf — via awesome-zsh-plugins
item.description: A plugin that completes ansible-playbook tags and works with fzf-tab.
